cards.explanation: The answer is new heavens and a new earth. The LORD says, "For behold, I will create new heavens and a new earth." (Isaiah 65:17) He doesn't say He'll patch up the old ones, friends. He says He'll create new ones.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "The former things will not be remembered, nor will they come to mind." So they won't still come to mind, friends. When the new heavens and new earth come, the old things aren't hanging around in anyone's thoughts.
The answer is forever. The LORD says, "But be glad and rejoice forever in what I create…" Forever is a long time to rejoice, friends. I can't even keep a good mood going through one burnt tray.

The answer is the LORD Himself. He says, "I will rejoice in Jerusalem and take delight in My people." So the LORD is the one rejoicing here, friends. He's glad over the city and the people He's creating.

The answer is weeping and crying. The LORD says, "The sounds of weeping and crying will no longer be heard in her." The city is Jerusalem, and those are the sounds that stop. I think that's a sound nobody will miss.

The answer is a hundred. The LORD says, "For the youth will die at a hundred years…" So in this picture, someone who reaches a hundred is still called a youth, friends. That's a long, full life, and the verse treats it as just the start of the picture.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "…he who fails to reach a hundred will be considered accursed." Think about what the verse just said before it: no more infants living only a few days. In this picture, a life that falls short of a hundred is the thing that stands out as unusual. That's how long the LORD says His people's days will be.
The answer is live in them. The LORD says, "They will build houses and dwell in them…" The ones who build the houses are the ones who live in them, friends. I'd call that a fair deal.

The answer is a tree. The LORD says, "For as is the lifetime of a tree, so will be the days of My people…" A tree can stand a long, long time, friends. That's the picture He gives for His people's days.
The answer is False. The LORD says, "They will not labor in vain…" The work counts, friends. In verse 22 He says His chosen ones "…will fully enjoy the work of their hands."

The answer is that they will be blessed by the LORD. He says, "for they will be a people blessed by the LORD…" That comes right after He says they won't bear children doomed to disaster, friends. He adds, "…they and their descendants with them."

The answer is False. The LORD says, "Even before they call, I will answer, and while they are still speaking, I will hear." So He doesn't wait for them to finish, friends. He answers before they call, and He hears while they are still speaking. I find that comforting.
The answer is the lamb. The LORD says, "The wolf and the lamb will feed together…" Normally a wolf and a lamb don't share a meal, friends. In this picture they eat side by side.
The answer is True. The LORD says, "…the lion will eat straw like the ox…" A lion eating straw is quite a picture, friends. It's part of the same scene as the wolf and the lamb feeding together.
The answer is True. The LORD says, "They will neither harm nor destroy on all My holy mountain…" Neither harm nor destruction, friends, and it covers the whole mountain. That's how the passage ends.
